speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are presenting with a rash on your scalp and forehead; can you tell me how long you have had these symptoms and if they are itchy or painful?

speaker: Patient
text: 3-month-old boy. The parents report that the rash has been present for several weeks, noting that it sometimes appears red and scaly, especially during cold weather. The patient was born at 36 weeks' gestation and has been generally healthy since. The patient's father has a history of psoriasis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Infantile Seborrheic Dermatitis (Cradle Cap).

I note the infant is 3 months old with a red, scaly rash that worsens in cold weather, which is classic for this condition despite the family history of psoriasis. Since this is a benign, self-limiting condition common in this age group, no further imaging or specialized tests are required at this time. I will recommend gentle cleansing with baby oil to soften the scales and frequent shampooing with a mild, hypoallergenic cleanser. If the rash spreads to the ears or eyelids or if the skin becomes oozing, please return for a re-evaluation to rule out a secondary bacterial infection.
